# dMod2

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/dModverse/dMod2/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/dModverse/dMod2/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-dmodverse.github.io%2FdMod2-blue)](https://dmodverse.github.io/dMod2/)
<!-- badges: end -->

dMod2 is a framework for dynamic modeling and parameter estimation in R. Reaction networks
become ODE models compiled to C/C++, with exact first- and second-order sensitivities. Prediction
functions, observation functions and parameter transformations are function objects composed
into a model of the data, and objective functions are minimized by multi-start fits with a
trust-region optimizer. Profile likelihoods, prediction uncertainty, steady states,
structural identifiability, mixed-effects models and interfaces to SBML and PEtab are part of
the package. The ODE backend is cppDE.

dMod2 succeeds dMod. [Migrating from dMod](https://dmodverse.github.io/dMod2/articles/migrating.html)
lists what a dMod script has to change.

## Installation

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("dModverse/dMod2")
```

cppDE is installed with it. Models are compiled at run time and need a C++17 compiler (Rtools
on Windows) and Python with SymPy, which reticulate provides on first use.

## Citation

There is no publication for dMod2 yet. `citation("dMod2")` gives the paper on the predecessor
dMod, the reference for the modeling framework: Kaschek D, Mader W, Fehling-Kaschek M,
Rosenblatt M, Timmer J (2019). Dynamic Modeling, Parameter Estimation, and Uncertainty Analysis
in R. *Journal of Statistical Software*, 88(10), 1-32, DOI 10.18637/jss.v088.i10.
